Florida

6 directory entries · Research in progress

  • Calusa↗Historical homeland connection
    Connection & source
    Historical homeland connection

    Actual NPS first geography paragraph locates Calusa along southwest Florida coast. Other stereotypes, population estimates and material-culture claims not adopted.

    Historical southwest Florida community-region connection. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Miccosukee↗Tribe published historical homeland connection
    Connection & source
    Tribe published historical homeland connection

    The tribal enterprise's history explicitly describes Miccosukee ancestral towns in northern Florida and later camps in southern Florida's Everglades. Only the Florida connection is indexed; other historical identity arguments are not generalized.

    Public content inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Pensacola↗Historical Panzacola people connection in original scholarly research
    Connection & source
    Historical Panzacola people connection in original scholarly research

    DeRoche’s introduction explicitly places the historical Panzacola people around present-day Pensacola Bay in West Florida using seventeenth-century documentary accounts. His discussion distinguishes this people from the archaeological Pensacola culture; the test excavation did not establish a positive Panzacola site identification. Inspection: Actual university public download, valid-TLS HTTP 200, 2,675,875 bytes, 100 PDF pages including added cover. Cover/title; abstract printed p.viii / PDF p.9; introduction printed pp.1–3 / PDF pp.10–12; and printed p.8 / PDF p.17 were read as text/OCR. Not a complete thesis or excavation-data review. Limits: The canonical name Pensacola is retained; Panzacola is the historical people-label used by the thesis. The later city and archaeological culture are separate referents. No definitive excavated Panzacola village, coordinates, ethnicity-from-ceramics inference, contemporary recognition status or disappearance claim is adopted. This is an original student thesis with committee oversight, not a statement of consensus on every historical identification.

    Seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries, especially documentary accounts of the 1680s–1690s. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗

    Connection & source
    Historical and continuing homeland connection

    Seminole Tribe of Florida narrative identifies Florida as homeland; not interchangeable with separate Miccosukee or Oklahoma governments.

    Historical and continuing; inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

  • Timucua↗Documented historical language area connection
    Connection & source
    Documented historical language area connection

    NPS explicitly identifies northern Florida among the historical Timucua-speaking areas and notes that the communities were politically distinct. The umbrella directory name does not imply one Timucua government.

    Public content inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

  • Yamasee↗Historical refuge / migration connection
    Connection & source
    Historical refuge / migration connection

    The account describes Yamasee near St. Augustine before migration to Carolina and refuge with Spanish St. Augustine after the war. Inspection: Historic context E pp. 3 and 6. Limits: Historical Florida connection; not exclusive homeland or present government location.

    Late seventeenth century and after the 1715 Yamasee War. Reviewed 2026-10-21.
